rows.question: Under the UCB directions, can a UCB levy pre-payment charges on a floating rate loan to an individual for non-business purposes sanctioned in March 2026?
rows.answer: No: for a UCB, pre-payment charges are not permitted on all floating rate loans granted for purposes other than business to individuals, with or without co-obligant(s), when the loan is sanctioned or renewed on or after 1 January 2026.  The older pre-payment-charge directions were withdrawn or repealed and are no longer in force on 2026-11-23.

rows.question: Can a Tier 3 UCB levy a pre-payment charge on a Rs 80 lakh floating-rate business loan to an MSE proprietor sanctioned on 15 March 2026?
rows.answer: For a floating-rate business loan sanctioned on or after 1 January 2026 to an MSE, a Tier 3 UCB shall not levy pre-payment charges only where the sanctioned amount or limit is up to ₹50 lakh. [E6, E8] In cases other than those covered by that no-charge rule, pre-payment charges, if any, shall be as per the approved policy of the UCB, and for term loans they shall be based on the amount being prepaid. [E10, E11] The charge also must be clearly disclosed in the sanction letter and loan agreement, and a charge that was not disclosed as specified there shall not be charged. [E15, E17]

rows.question: Does section 8.2 of our Retail Loan Policy on penal interest comply with RBI's penal charges rules?
rows.answer: Section 8.2 is in force and says penal interest at 2% per month over the applicable rate of interest shall be charged on overdue instalments and compounded monthly. For a UCB, the current RBI directions say penal interest is not permitted. So section 8.2 does not comply with the current RBI rule on penal interest because it imposes penal interest rather than penal charges. The older RBI circulars on penal charges also said the penalty should be treated as penal charges and not levied as penal interest, but those circulars are no longer in force on 2026-11-23.
